predecessors.name: Mongol Empire
predecessors.text: the Qara Khitai lands Chagatai inherited in 1227

successors.name: Chagatai Khanate
successors.text: Transoxiana and the Tarim Basin, carried on by Duwa

successors.name: Ögedeid ulus
successors.text: the east of Transoxania and the Bukhara region, ceded to Kaidu in the peace of c.1267 and handed over here in 1271, when the Ogedeid ulus is formed

ledger.x: 1227: Chagatai inherits the Qara Khitai lands.
1260: Ariq Böke names Alghu head of the Chagatai ulus.
c.1263: Alghu takes Otrar and Khorazm from Berke's Golden Horde.
1266: Baraq breaks with Kublai over the Tarim Basin.
c.1267: Otrar and Khwarazm return to the Jochids.
22 July 1270: Baraq is beaten at Herat.
1271 (the peace dates from c.1267): Semirechye and the Bukhara region pass to Kaidu.
1271: the Chagatai khans become Kaidu's clients.
1289: the Tarim Basin passes to Kaidu and Duwa.
1293: bookkeeping hand-over, not an end of the relation.
1293: the ulus carries on as the Chagatai Khanate.

wars.name: Toluid Civil War (Chagatai front)
wars.outcome: Kublai won. Alghu, Ariq's appointee, turned on Ariq in 1262-63; Ariq took Almalikh and Alghu fled to Samarkand in 1263; Ariq surrendered at Shangdu in 1264; Alghu died in 1265.

wars.name: Baraq–Kaidu war
wars.outcome: Kaidu, helped by Möngke-Temür's Golden Horde army, beat Baraq near Khujand; Baraq kept two thirds of Transoxiana and gave up the east and the Bukhara region at the peace of c.1267 (or 1269).

wars.name: Baraq’s invasion of the Ilkhanate
wars.outcome: Baraq beat the governor Buchin in Khorasan, then lost to Abaqa near Herat on 22 July 1270 and retreated to Bukhara; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Ilkhanid invasion of Transoxiana
wars.outcome: Abaqa 'invaded Transoxania in 1272 and sacked Bukhara, carrying off 50,000 captives' (Chagatai page); a raid, no land changed hands.

wars.name: Kaidu–Kublai war (Chagatai side)
wars.outcome: 'In 1275, Duwa joined Kaidu in the war against the Yuan dynasty but were repelled' (Chagatai page); the Yuan left the Tarim in 1288/89.

certainty.note: Steppe, oasis and mountain frontiers throughout; no treaty line is recorded.
